newsitem.title: USA: U.S., German leaders meet on WTO, procurement.
newsitem.headline: U.S., German leaders meet on WTO, procurement.

text.p: Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and German Economic State Secretary Lorenz Schomerus held talks Thursday on two trade issues, a U.S. spokeswoman said.

The officials discussed Germany's plan to assure open competition in its heavy electrical equipment market and the first meeting trade ministers under the aegis of the World Trade Organization, set for December in Singapore.
A Barshefsky aide described the meeting as "cordial."
On Tuesday, Barshefsky delayed implementation of sanctions because Germany had agreed to reform its procurement system for heavy electrical equipment.

Barshefsky said the United States would closely monitor efforts to put the reforms into law. Sanctions were possible if there were unreasonable delays in action on the reforms or if U.S. firms ran into discrimination while the legislation was pending.
The meeting with Schomerus was expected to provide details of the reform plan.
